enunciado: Let \(k\) be a given positive integer with \(k\geqslant2\). Prove that the product of three consecutive positive integers cannot be the \(k\) -th power of an integer.

Let $n$ be a fixed positive integer. Determine the smallest possible rank of an $n \times n$ matrix that has zeros along the main diagonal and strictly positive real numbers off the main diagonal.
 Prove that the answer is: 3

The generic rank of a $4 \times m \times m$ tensor is $\lceil 4m^2 / (2m + 2) \rceil$
[Fri12, (5.7)]. This is the case $(4, m, m)$ of `isGenericRank_of_le_critical`, settled in
[AOP09]; see [BFZ24, Section 4.5].

The trivial upper bound, by counting pairs of points: for $k \geq 2$,
$$f_k(n) \cdot k(k-1) \leq n(n-1).$$
